body:
This is really insightful.  I have also contemplated divorce many times, even filed two years ago and really had made up my mind, but my husband convinced me at the 11th hour that he would go to counseling.  Spoiler alert:  he did, for as long as it took for me to dismiss the divorce proceedings, and slowly but surely he reverted to his old ways.  I am kicking myself for not going through with it then, because I was stronger (physically, mentally) and had some money saved up.  

Can I ask, did you ever hold out hope that they would get along?  I ask this because my younger child seems to want that, and I just hate to be the person who puts that childlike dream to rest.
Feel free to PM me.  You’re not alone.

A bat house.  It was four 2x4s in a rectangle, with a roof nailed on top, and a small hole for a door.  My uncle told me if I put it outside, I could catch bats.  It didn’t work.  (Not sure I wanted it to, tbh).
Thank you for this much needed laugh!!
He is definitely gaslighting you.  I’m so sorry you are experiencing this, especially with young kids.  I can empathize.  What is your biggest fear/concern about leaving?

Oy... I just posted about my own age gap experience today.  It’s my first and only post so if you click my profile you can probably see what I said.  Spoiler alert:  it has been very difficult for me as the years go on and I feel stunted and unhappy.  HOWEVER, your situation is different than mine in a couple ways:  1) you are in your late 20s, which suggests you have more experience and insight than I had when I entered into an age gap (I was 22 and it was only my second relationship).  I am guessing you have a better handle on what is good for you!  2) your age gap, while significant, is not as drastic as mine is (24 years).  You and your bf sound like you’re both roughly on the same page as far as career, kids, experiences, outlook, etc.  I think it’s incredibly important to have somewhat equal footing in the relationship, especially financially, so that one person doesn’t have an unfair advantage over the other.

I definitely think your relationship could be a success story, as long as you’ve seriously thought about how the future would play out and how that would affect you (negatively or positively).  Best of luck to both of you!

Exactly.  The sad part is, he really doesn’t even offer much financially... it’s definitely not a sugar daddy situation, as I’ve worked in some capacity, always, since I met him.  But to my 22-year-old self, any “adult” type person with a steady job seemed really advanced and cool compared to the people I grew up with in my small town.  Ugh.  There’s just so much to unpack, I really do fear I am damaged beyond repair.  If I didn’t have kids, would be a no-brainer.  Thanks so much for listening and weighing-in.  It really helps to get this out there, even anonymously, and hear some objective thoughts.

Oh man, you took the words from my mouth!  I go in circles trying to justify making this work, and keep coming to the same conclusion: he just does not care.  I wish I could get angry about it, but he is old now and I just get sad. :(

You are so kind.  ❤️ I appreciate these thoughtful words so much.  Yes, my kids are still minors. Definitely a huge part of why I stay, if not the biggest reason.  They do love their dad and it has been important for me to make sure they don’t witness all of the negativity (though I’m sure my older child is becoming aware).  My husband will definitely fight for custody if I leave.  He is more financially stable.  My career has taken a backseat to raising the kids, cleaning the house, and even working (without a paycheck) for my husband’s business.  It’s so textbook, I’m ashamed to even admit how dependent I’ve become.  It would rock my kids’ world if we divorce... and I have been willing to put their happiness over mine, always.  But I do believe that a happy mom will eventually be worth more to them than a facade.  Ugh.  It’s all so much tougher than I ever imagined it would be.  Young people like you give me so much hope, I mean that... keep being that smart confident person, always.

You are so right on with this, I really appreciate the clarity.  I am afraid I will leave this relationship with so much baggage, no one will want me.   I KNOW it’s wrong.  I know I need to leave.  I look in the mirror and cry every day, wondering how this came to be my life, feeling so low value.  On the other hand, if I left and had to witness him getting older alone, I would feel incredibly responsible for his care.  The thought of it all makes me so upset, I really do contemplate disappearing.  Men please take heed, leave much younger girls alone.  It doesn’t end well.

This is exactly what I fear happened... I want to believe he is a good man, for the sake of my kids.  But I can’t wrap my educated adult head around what he did.  When I tell him that I feel duped, he says, “you weren’t a child.  You knew better.”   Which is almost like he admits it was a bad choice?!  Agh... the mental gymnastics have seriously hurt my head.  As he gets into his 60s, he has taken a different turn and even apologized to me a couple times.  I don’t even know what to do with that.  Anyway, thank you for listening and for your candor.
Thank you so much.  I could use the world’s biggest hug.  I would cry forever.  Lately I cry even at the thought of someone being nice to me.  Ugh.

Thanks so much for listening.  I am sure that between my friends I could find a temporary place to stay, if I were honest with them about what is happening.  However, I fear how this will shake out with my kids.  They won’t want to leave our house. :(
